text: This app has unprecedented flexibility and I'm impressed with number of useful features (unlike other apps with fancy but useless features) ... YT tutorials for an app seemed overkill at first but are very useful to understand amazing potential of this app ... Bought the pro ver and I intend use this to get my work on track :) Though it can still be improved and here are few suggestions ... Also in case my suggestions are invalid, I hope I can get some clarification on tool usage. .............. [A] Tasks under a scheduled activity have to be marked completed separately from activity time log. I believe, once time log is completed, app can ask about if linked tasks have been completed (Just like how deleting activity deletes related tasks). Otherwise we end up with zombie tasks (for both single & repeated schedule). Option to hide tasks under activities or some visual indication that they are under this activity may help I guess .............. [B] Parent category doesn't take into account activities or tasks of its children. Not sure if its intended but my programmer brain seems to work that way :P. Eg: I wanted to make a general activity as 'Morning Routine' (for Home) and have tasks from all sub categories in it. .............. [C] I believe definition of tasks and activities becomes confusing for most people. I keep on thinking that tasks can be sub activities under a scheduled activity. But its not the case in tutorial. This can be powerful for some folks but can be confusing (atleast for me) .............. [D] Not sure why an activity's time type can't be changed after creation. Atleast a switch between time range/time amount should be possible since plans may change (Or when I try to be less lazy and want to commit to a time for workout later on :P) .............. [E] (*minor knitpicking) UI Scales for mobile may get bit too small to use at times (have a Oneplus 3T)
author: Akshay Dharmadhikari
developer_reply: Thanks a lot Akshay! Here I'm limited to 350 symbols, so can't answer to everything. Anyway, tasks and activities can be completed in different time, thus it should be an option; deleting an activity does not delete a task; I will make changing the activity type possible; and you can use a pinch gesture for scaling ) Please stand with my Ukraine!

text: This app is ambitious and needs significant work in English translation to make it usable without going to the Wiki or a combination of lots of both time to mess with the app and previous experience with similar option-rich productivity apps  time.  But, I think there might be something special here, so while I rarely rate or review apps and never subscribe unless totally "sold" on an app, I made an exemption here.  The wiki tutorials clearly show the developers are trying hard to clarify how to use the app. They wrote not one but FIVE variations of the tutorial, each for a different  domains of life. I was so thrilled to see one specifically tailored for how to manage housework, that I decided to subscribe for 3 months, so I could offer feedback and a little financial support. Developers, please prioritize a language overhaul in English. With years as an ESOL teacher with a progressive attitude about English as spoken by non-native speakers, I still struggled to understand the basic terminology essential to the app and after much time had to go to the Wiki for a tutorial.  I should not have to use the Wiki for BASIC clarification. Though he admits the language is unintuitive, Oleksander Abul dissed the comments of a reviewer with a similar complaint by stating there is no need to go to the Wiki if one spends "at least 10 minutes playing around" with it. What about all the people who got frustrated and deleted the app without reviewing? Or people who downloaded it, spent too much time trying to figure it out then back burner it indefinitely?  This is not a game. It is a productivity app. No one should have to spend the minimum of 10 minutes trying to figure out what basic terms mean.  A primary goal of a successful app is to make it as intuitive as possible. No need for whistles and bells until you have a sound wagon to ride in.   This is an app about planning and prioritizing time. Please developers, think about this. Think of the amount of time ultimately gained by prioritizing fixing the "unintuitive language" problem.  Think of your time. Think of all the people potentially downloading your app because they value time.  Looking at your Wiki I see a team willing to commit time and thought to this app. I am sure I am not the only person willing to volunteer to help you make the language more clear so this app can become as good as it deserves to be.
author: A Google user

Yes, we've spent an enormous amount of time trying to make the wording as accurate as possible, but seems like we still haven't succeeded in it. text: This is literally my dream app, and the only reason I have not bought it yet is because I am in-between jobs right now and can't afford it.   This is, without a doubt, the best Organization App I have ever had the pleasure to use. I won't lie, there is a bit of a learning curve to it.  The strength of this app is not as a task manager or an agenda, although it's main function is closely tied to them. It's main function is as an "Intent tracker", meaning that you program your intent for the day, and then you track how long you actually kept that intent on the day.  This is extremely ussefull, as it forces you to face what you are actually doing with your time, and makes you reflect what is really important and what you want to accomplish.  It even has a comparison chart of what your intents are vs. what intents you actually  do.  Of course, as a planner app you still have the common lists and tasks. Unfortunately this app doesn't have subtasks as a default, however you can use subtasks up to three levels to create tasks inside tasks. Another thing is the priority system and filter, which makes it really easy to categorize what is really important
